fields.value: Dental implant treatment at Tooth n Care

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: An implant is a titanium post placed in the jaw that acts as a new tooth root, topped with a crown made to match. It stands on its own, without leaning on neighbouring teeth.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Implants are not a quick fix, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling. Most cases run three to six months from placement to final crown, because the bone needs time to bond to the post.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Examination and a 3D CBCT scan here in the practice, to measure bone height, width and where the nerves and sinuses sit.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The titanium post is placed under local anaesthetic, usually in under an hour. Most people are surprised how straightforward the day itself is.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Three to six months while bone integrates with the post. A temporary tooth can usually be worn in the meantime.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: An abutment is fitted and a custom crown made to match your other teeth in shape and shade, then screwed or cemented into place.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Implants have a high success rate, but they are surgery and they are not for everyone. You should know all of this before you decide:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Swelling, bruising and discomfort for several days after placement

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Infection, or failure of the post to integrate - occasionally requiring removal and a second attempt

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Damage to nerves, sinuses or adjacent teeth - the reason we scan in 3D first

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Peri-implantitis, a gum and bone infection around the implant, if cleaning slips

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Smoking, uncontrolled diabetes and some medications measurably raise failure rates

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Insufficient bone may mean a graft first, adding months and cost

fields.label: List item
fields.value: The crown will still need maintenance, and can chip or loosen over the years

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: An implant isn’t the only answer

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Fixed, quicker and usually cheaper, but it requires cutting down the teeth either side. Sensible when those teeth already need crowns; wasteful when they’re pristine.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Removable, far cheaper, and useful while you decide or save. Less stable, and takes getting used to.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Sometimes reasonable, particularly for a back tooth. But neighbouring teeth drift and the opposing tooth over-erupts, so it isn’t cost-free either. We’ll be straight with you about which applies.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What it costs, before it starts

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Every treatment plan we give you carries its price, its inclusions and any conditions in writing before you agree to anything. Implants are a larger investment than most dental treatment, and health fund rebates vary widely by policy. Compassionate Release of Super through the ATO can apply to implants and dentures for essential treatment.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Bring your card and we claim through HICAPS at the desk, so you only pay the gap. All funds welcome, including HCF, Bupa, Medibank, nib, CBHS, Teachers Health, Defence Health, Australian Unity and GMHBA.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: First visit with us? Exam, treatment plan, X-rays, scale and clean and fluoride are no-gap where your fund rebates $199 or more, or a flat $199 without cover. New patients only; a $50 booking deposit applies and comes off the visit.
